title: Welsh Rarebit
subtitle: Cheese and beer sauce on toast, grilled until bubbling
excerpt: Welsh rarebit is a savoury cheese sauce , cheddar melted with beer, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce , spread on toast and grilled until golden and bubbling. It is one of the oldest recorded British savouries and one of the best uses of strong cheese. The sauce must be thick enough to sit on the bread without running, and the grill must be hot.
sourceNotes: Welsh rarebit (also written rabbit) is one of the oldest dishes in the British canon, first recorded in the early eighteenth century. It was originally a savoury cheese sauce on toast, and the name refers to an ironic joke about Welsh poverty, implying that cheese was what the Welsh ate when they could not afford meat.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the cheese sauce up to 3 days ahead and refrigerate. Spread and grill on the day.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cooked mixture of equal parts flour and butter that forms the base for a thickened sauce. The flour and butter are cooked together first, then liquid is added gradually.

content.text: Welsh rarebit is not just cheese on toast. The cheese is melted into a sauce with beer, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce, then spread thickly on toast and grilled. The sauce should be thick and barely pourable, not runny. Use the strongest cheddar you can find: the flavour dilutes slightly as it is spread and grilled.

items.prepNote: thick slices, toasted on one side only

content.text: Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir in {{plain-flour}} of flour and cook for 1 minute to make a
. Gradually whisk in {{beer}} of ale or stout until smooth. Cook for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens. Remove from the heat.

Stir in {{cheddar}} of grated cheddar, {{english-mustard}} of English mustard, and {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce. Stir until the cheese melts completely and the sauce is smooth and thick. Season with pepper. Taste before adding salt: the cheese and Worcestershire sauce are already salty.

Heat the grill to its highest setting. Toast {{white-bread}} slices of bread on one side only. Spread the cheese sauce generously over the untoasted side: thick enough to hold its shape but spreadable.
Grill 10 to 15 cm from the heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce is deeply golden and bubbling at the edges. Watch closely: it goes from pale to burnt quickly. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: The sauce runs off the toast under the grill
items.cause: The sauce was too thin, or the bread was already fully toasted so it could not absorb any of the sauce.
items.fix: The sauce should be thick enough to need spreading rather than pouring. Toast the bread on one side only so the untoasted side grips the sauce.

items.cause: The cheese was added to a sauce that was too hot and the protein seized.
items.fix: Take the pan off the heat before adding the cheese. The residual heat is enough to melt it without the sauce splitting.

items.cause: A mild cheddar was used, or the Worcestershire sauce and mustard were underseasoned.
items.fix: Use the sharpest cheddar available. Both the mustard and the Worcestershire sauce should be noticeable, not just background.

items.symptom: The toast has gone soggy under the sauce
items.cause: The sauce was too runny, or the rarebit sat too long before grilling.
items.fix: Grill immediately after spreading. A thick sauce on one-side-toasted bread will not soak through before the grill sets the top.

content.text: Welsh rarebit is one of the oldest named dishes in British cooking. Recipes appear from the early eighteenth century. It is a dish where simple, cheap ingredients produce an outstanding result: strong cheese, good bread, a little beer. The name rabbit puzzles etymologists, but the dish itself does not. The quality of the cheese does all the work.
